Murmur · the architecture, its data, and one recorded evening

AI agents in every home, put to work on the grid's evening peak

The premise

AI agents will enter every household and every part of our lives, and make them run more efficiently.

The goal, for a utility company

Use those agents to shave the grid's peak: less draw from homes, buildings and other sites, from 18:00 to 21:00.

Payment

By delivery, on record

  1. The aggregator, such as ENGIE, asks for less draw from 18:00 to 21:00. It asks. It never orders.
  2. A community answers through its community agent, which turns its members' offers into one promise. A data center and a solar-and-battery plant each answer for themselves.
  3. Code decides every amount. AI has one part: reading what people write, and the words in reports.
  4. A guard checks every command before it reaches a device, and has the last word.
  5. Only amounts leave a site. Every message between owners crosses NANDA Town, signed.

The aggregator and the buyers

Reading cleanerML

Cleans the grid's readings before any plan is made.

ENGIE's own dataset
  • The loading of every transformer, hour by hour, for 2025.
  • ENGIE's 2023 release, where the true grid state is known. The cleaning is proven on it.
Sharing-outCODE

Works out the need by hour and shares it among all 80.

ENGIE's own dataset
  • Every participant's battery: power, energy, charge and connection limit.
  • How far a transformer's loading falls for each MW given at a site, fitted on the 2023 grid state.
Our own estimates
  • The line to stay under: 80% of a transformer's rating.
Request agentCODE
Sends each participant the sharing-out's figures, signed. It holds no data of its own.
RefereeCODE · AI

Checks every report row. A small model reads only the words.

ENGIE's own dataset
  • The report layout ENGIE's participants send: net power, charge, a quote and a note.
  • ENGIE's own 2025 reports, with the false ones they hold. The referee was built and measured on them.
Our own estimates
  • Its settings: every report is held against the meter at 30 minutes and at 2 hours.
  • The false reports planted in our own runs.
The buyers and their order

A utility and a grid operator order the cut. In the runs they are stand-ins.

ENGIE's own dataset
  • The window, 18:00 to 21:00: the three dearest hours in ENGIE's prices, in every month of 2025.
  • The community's connection limit, 3,214 kW.
Our own estimates
  • The price of a cut: $2.04 per kWh, our conversion of a Massachusetts programme's $275 per kW. Range $1.53 to $3.06.
  • The size of the order, set so that all that is offered is taken.
  • The pay split: 70% members, 10% the community's operator, 20% the aggregator.

The community and its agent

The community's own record

One of ENGIE's 20 communities is the host. Our homes and buildings sit inside it.

ENGIE's own dataset
  • Net power at its meter, every 15 minutes of 2025.
  • Its solar size, 3,416 kW, and its temperature, sunlight and prices.
Our own estimates
  • Its solar by day, estimated from ENGIE's 35 metered solar plants (R² 0.92).
  • The split of its use: our 200 homes 23%, our office 3%, our shops 6%. The other 68% stays as ENGIE recorded it.
Members' batteries

The homes' own batteries, held for the peak. The community has none of its own.

ENGIE's own dataset
  • ENGIE's one figure for the community's home batteries: 1,624 kW and 4,400 kWh, with their reported charge.
Community forecastML

What its members will draw and can give tomorrow evening.

ENGIE's own dataset
  • ENGIE's temperature and sunlight.
Our own estimates
  • Forecast models trained on our 200 homes.
  • For a building, the last day of the same kind.
Promise and coverCODE

Promises less than its members offered, in case they deliver less.

Our own estimates
  • The cover is taken from the community's own record of earlier evenings. Until three are on record it is a fixed 10%.
Clearing, gap filling, reportCODE

Clears the offers, fills gaps on the day, and reports upward.

ENGIE's own dataset
  • The report goes upward in ENGIE's own layout. No member is named in it.
Our own estimates
  • Each member's baseline: its ten most recent similar days, adjusted to the day itself.

Homes: 200 households, eight of them on the network

The house, its heating and coolingHARDWARE

A physics model of each house, checked against measured homes.

Public measured records
  • National Grid load research: the average Massachusetts home, hour by hour. Shape of the day r = 0.92.
  • A measured multi-story instrumented research house dataset, circuit-level heat pump, lighting, and plug loads: one measured house, its solar and its heat pump.
Our own estimates
  • Each house's physics: one thermal mass, heat loss 0.15 to 0.67 kW per °C.
Its devicesHARDWARE

Battery, car and charger, thermostat, water heater, dryer, dishwasher, pool pump.

Our product survey
  • 172 products of 108 brands in 22 kinds. Each rating comes from its maker's datasheet.
  • Seven battery products, and cars from 19 models.
Public measured records
  • Which home owns what: the federal household survey (EIA RECS 2024), Massachusetts single-family homes.
Our own estimates
  • A two-way car in every home at the full level. It is an ideal case: 34 of the 200 cars can power a home today.
The peoplePERSON

Who is home, what they allow, and what they write to their agent.

Our own estimates
  • Six household types, with the holidays and school breaks of 2025.
  • Each owner's limits: how much warmer the house may get, a car timer, devices that are off limits.
  • When cars leave, return and charge. No public measured home-charging data exists.
  • The notes the small model reads: written by us for the tests, each with its true meaning set down first.
The weather
ENGIE's own dataset
  • ENGIE's temperature and sunlight at its site.
Public measured records
  • A second version of the year adds the real day-to-day movement of measured Massachusetts weather.

Buildings: a small office and a strip of shops

Size, energy and shape of the dayHARDWARE

How much each building uses, and when.

ENGIE's own dataset
  • ENGIE's temperature and sunlight, as for the homes.
Public measured records
  • Boston's building energy reports (BERDO 2025). Our office matches 56 Boston offices, middle size 37,000 sq ft. Our shops match 8 strip malls and stores, 50,000 sq ft.
  • National Grid's business classes: the hourly shape of each building type.
  • Boston Public Library's meter, every 5 minutes: real day-to-day variation, from 380 usable days.
Its equipment and limitsHARDWARE

Cooling, fans, lights and plugs, and what each may do.

Our product survey
  • 145 products of 90 brands in 41 kinds.
  • 224 control rules, checked against makers' documents and the mechanical code. The guard keeps them.
Who is in, and wherePERSON
Our own estimates
  • An occupancy plan by zone, made the day before, and the day as it truly went.
  • How cooling, fans, lights and plugs split among zones: assigned by floor area. No public source gives it.
  • The manager's notes the small model reads: written by us for the tests.

Solar-and-battery plants and data centers

Each site's meter, battery and limitsHARDWARE

Each site answers the aggregator for itself.

ENGIE's own dataset
  • 50 plants and 10 data centers: net power and battery charge every 15 minutes, with each battery's power and energy and the site's connection limit.
A data center's work that can wait
ENGIE's own dataset
  • ENGIE's 2023 release: 16.3% of the data centers' energy can wait, for 4.5 to 10.5 hours.
Our own estimates
  • Its carry-over to the same sites' 2025 load.
A note from a person at a plantPERSON
Our own estimates
  • Three notes written by us for the test, each with its true meaning set down first.

The network and the payment

NANDA Town
MIT's NANDA Town, run locally. It carries signed envelopes and reads nothing inside. It is software, and holds no data.
Readings, settlement, payment
Our own estimates
  • The meters are the simulated devices' own. A twin of each home and building with no sale gives the truth.
  • Pay follows delivery against the baseline, at the price above.

One recorded evening

28 January 2025, on ENGIE's data. Eight homes, two buildings, the community agent, three single sites and the aggregator's agent ran as separate programs. NANDA Town carried every signed message between them.

1 of 38136 kW
Two buyers order the same evening

A utility and a grid operator each order a cut from 18:00 to 21:00: 136 kW in all, for each half hour.

1 of 8or the ← → keysOpen the full replay

  1. A utility and a grid operator each order a cut from 18:00 to 21:00: 136 kW in all, for each half hour.

  2. Ten members offer 110 kW. The community agent promises 100 kW upward and keeps the rest as cover, in case its members deliver less.

  3. Next afternoon the aggregator plans. The grid needs 342 MW less at 19:00 and all 80 batteries can give 244, so each is asked for all it has. This community's part is 1,624 kW.

  4. The request crosses NANDA Town as a signed message, and the community agent takes it. An hour earlier a planted request, for twice the batteries' rating, was refused in writing.

  5. The same signed request goes to two solar-and-battery plants and a data center, with no coordinator in between. The largest plant is asked for 9.9 MW at 19:00.

  6. At 18:00 the community draws 92 kW less than its twin with no sale: 72 from homes and 20 from buildings.

  7. Every quarter hour each participant reports upward, signed. The referee holds every row to its checks: 155 of 155 are trusted, and nothing is held back.

  8. $497.07 for 294 kWh, at our assumed price. $347.95 of it goes to the members, by what each delivered.

854signed messages over NANDA Town, and no signature failed
468 of 468report rows from the three single sites, each as the plan expected
98 kWpromised on average over the evening, and 98 kW delivered on the buyers' meters
155 of 155of the community's report rows trusted by the referee

More recordings, made the same way: the same evening with twelve single sites, and one evening in each month of 2025 on ENGIE's own weather or on real day-to-day weather. On ENGIE's weather those twelve evenings carried 4,240 signed messages, and no signature failed. How the homes and devices are simulated is set out in the method note.

5

What is real

Said once, in one place.

Real

ENGIE's 2025 records, and our code. Each agent is a separate program. Their messages are signed and cross a NANDA Town run on one computer. A real small model reads the notes people write.

Simulated

Homes, buildings and their devices, each from a real product's ratings. A command travels the road it would travel to real equipment. Only the last step, the driver, is simulated.

Replayed

The members' batteries and the single sites' own power, from ENGIE's record.

Stand-ins and assumptions

The buyers and the aggregator's own agent are stand-ins. The price of a cut, $2.04 per kWh, is ours, with a range of $1.53 to $3.06.

Murmur, 20 November 2026. Figures come from ENGIE's 2025 dataset, the product catalogue, and the evening recorded on 20 November 2026.
